title: Runtime config combinators notebook
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad for a small DSL and API shape that lets us compose runtime configuration pieces (policies, batchers, quant profiles, KV-cache hints) using combinators instead of monolithic blobs. Aim: make overrides predictable, composable across scopes (global, tenant, route, canary).

Top-level idea (notes-to-self):
- Treat config as a series of small sealed fragments (combinators) with typed merge semantics.
- Each fragment has: id, type, priority, predicate, patch payload (JSON patch-ish), safety tags.
- Combinators are applied in order of scope (global -> region -> tenant -> route -> request) and then by explicit priority numeric.
- Default semantics: non-conflicting fields merge; conflicting scalar fields use last-writer-wins unless a 'guard' combinator vetoes.

ASCII diagram:

  +-----------------+    +----------------+    +-----------------+
  | Global profile  | -> | Tenant overlay | -> | Route override  |
  +-----------------+    +----------------+    +-----------------+
           |                      |                      |
           v                      v                      v
  runtime apply pipeline  ->  validator ->  safety checks -> final runtime config

API sketch (very rough):
POST /v1/runtime/config/apply
Body: {
  "selector": {"scope":"route","route_id":"chat.generate"},
  "combinators": [
    {"id":"global-batching-v2","type":"batching:profile","priority":10,"payload":{...}},
    {"id":"tenant-caching-hints","type":"cache:kv-hint","priority":20,"predicate":{"tenant":"ten-123"},"payload":{...}}
  ],
  "dry_run": true
}

Combinator types (brain dump):
- batching:profile  => continuous-batching windows, max tokens per batch, latency SLO hints
- cache:kv-hint     => prefix TTL, warmup keys, slice-to-shard hint
- quant:profile     => target bits (8/4), fallback model variant id
- routing:policy    => prefer region, tier fallback order
- guard:assertion   => predicate and fail_behavior (warn | block | escalate)

Merge rules (sketch):
- Layers applied scope->priority->insertion-order.
- For structured objects: use shallow-merge, then run validator to ensure invariants (e.g., batch.window_ms >= 1).
- Guard combinators evaluated after merge to veto unsafe combos (e.g., quant=4 + kv-cache enabled -> block for model-x).

Safety guardrails (operational):
- Every combinator document must list allowed model families and a risk category (low/medium/high).
- On apply, run a lightweight simulation: estimate token throughput, estimate GPU memory delta for KV/quant changes. If delta > threshold, require canary tag.
- Canary rollout combinator: attaches a traffic-split predicate {"percent": 5, "selector": "tenant"} and auto-escalation policy.

Validation heuristics to implement in runtime:
- static schema validation (JSON Schema for combinator types)
- cross-field heuristics (if batching.window_ms < 5ms and batch.size > 1024 -> warn)
- compatibility matrix lookup (model-family x quant profile -> allowed/unsupported)

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to store combinators historically? Append-only log (immutable) vs mutable versioned documents? Prefer append-only with compacting snapshots.
- UI: show effective diff per request (like git merge but for runtime config) — expensive to compute per request, maybe cache per route + change-id.
- How to express negative/withdraw combinators (undo a previous patch)? Maybe a tombstone combinator with target id.
- Can we leverage existing rollout infra (A/B engine) for traffic-split semantics or do we need a lightweight copy?

Local testing notes:
- small shim cli: ./tools/runtime-config-sim --base ./snapshots/global.json --apply ./combinator-sets/dev.json --selector route:chat.generate --dry-run
- unit tests: combinator merge order, guard evaluation, canary escalate path

Benchmarks to collect:
- cost of merge/validate on 1k tenants with 10 combinators each (target < 20ms apply).
- simulation memory delta estimation speed (< 5ms ideally).

Random thoughts: keep combinator payloads small. Prefer references to larger artifacts (e.g., quant profile id references a stored artifact) instead of embedding heavy arrays inlined.

References: linked PR above has proto sketches and a proto route for "combinator". Might adapt existing admission controller hooks rather than reimplement.

Notes-to-self: iterate API shape to support PATCH semantics (apply, preview, list-resolved) and a separate endpoint for canary progression callbacks. Keep first iteration internal API-only behind flag.

End of scratchpad.
